method.statement: candidate.in-transaction.sql sent byte-exact through the connector's apply_migration (the connector adds its own transaction and the ledger insert). The packaged candidate.sql carries its own transaction control (a begin; as line 6 and a commit; as the last line), which would nest inside and close the connector's own transaction early. The statement sent is therefore candidate.sql without exactly those two lines (candidate.in-transaction.sql, derived in this checkout by dropping line 6 and the last line; candidate.sql 41494 bytes, md5 4f3c30356af57ec8c11c224c5aad65e6, sha256 554faa74f2149d86... equal to the manifest; the derived file 41479 bytes, 497 lines, pure ASCII, md5 b807226efc56b7ce89ad1ce5e2ebf381). It was sent byte-exact and the stored statement was read back from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations afterwards: 1 statement, 41479 characters (41479 bytes), md5 b807226efc56b7ce89ad1ce5e2ebf381, equal to the derived file.
method.insideTheStatement: Pre-guards in the same transaction: certificate ready; the two helpers absent; MATCH-V1's three rule functions pinned by body md5; the reader's predecessor md5. The reader replacement: preimage md5, exactly one anchor of the old body in pg_get_functiondef, then the new body md5 dc69802e3ba209232a8be095f60e9c9f, the whole pg_proc row apart from the body and the function comment asserted unchanged (so SECURITY INVOKER, STABLE and the ACL stay). Post-guards: the two helpers pinned by md5 with security definer, stable, owner postgres, search_path=pg_catalog and ACL {postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres}; the reader ACL unchanged; both closure digests equal before and after (a temporary table of the pre-apply digests) and the certificate ready. Any difference aborts and rolls back.
